items.title: Defining collectivism as duties in relationships rather than generalized warmth improves predictive validity in 100 cultures
items.author: Timo von Oertzen
items.content: Talhelm et al. propose responsibilism as a specific conceptualization of collectivism that emphasizes responsibilities, duties and roles in close relationships. The responsibilism scale effectively captures cross-cultural differences.

items.title: Large estimated size of the Australian Indigenous population before its extensive decline following colonial invasion
items.author: Corey J. A. Bradshaw
items.content: Before the British invasion in 1788, Australia’s Indigenous population is estimated to have numbered about 2.2 million people, exceeding previous estimates. An estimated 2.06 million excess deaths occurred between 1788 and 1861.

items.title: Building health-literate artificial intelligence
items.author: Ruth M. Parker
items.content: Can AI do more than deliver health information? This Perspective argues that AI should be designed to support understanding, informed decision-making and action, placing health literacy at the centre of AI design and governance.

items.title: Complexity is a unified cognitive kind
items.author: Chaz Firestone
items.content: Boger and Firestone show that humans possess a domain-general, cross-modal representation of complexity.

items.title: Loneliness and desire for thinness explain sex differences in adolescent internalizing problems
items.author: Koutarou Takada
items.content: Girls tend to show higher rates of depression and suicidal ideation than boys. This work suggests that loneliness and pressure to be thin explain much of this gap, suggesting that social factors are key targets for youth-focused support, policy and intervention.

items.title: Staying in academia after extended leave
items.author: Theresa Mercer
items.content: Returning to academia after extended leave often depends on luck and goodwill. We need better and formalized systems to facilitate returns and retention, argues Theresa Mercer.
